bear.argument: NKE's fiscal 2026 filing shows a business under strain. Net income fell 3% to $3,108 million from $3,219 million, and EBIT margin was 8.3%, versus 12.7% two years earlier in fiscal 2024. Revenue fell 10% in fiscal 2024 and was essentially flat in fiscal 2026 at $46.4 billion, down 2% on a currency-neutral basis. Greater China revenue declined 11% and Converse revenue fell 31%, with Converse EBIT down 93% to $18 million. Management says negative impacts from Greater China and Converse will continue throughout fiscal 2027. Operating cash flow fell from $3,698 million to $2,868 million. NIKE Brand Digital sales dropped 12% on a currency-neutral basis, and the company is marking down inventory to clear it. The $986 million IEEPA tariff recovery flattered cost of sales, so underlying profitability is weaker than reported net income suggests. Shares repurchases were paused, and the company faces ongoing securities class actions.

Management expects revenue headwinds from Greater China and Converse to persist into fiscal 2027.
claims.quote: We expect negative impacts from Greater China and Converse to continue throughout fiscal 2027.

claims.claim: Operating cash flow declined meaningfully year over year.
claims.quote: In fiscal 2026, cash provided by operations was $2,868 million.

bull.argument: The bull case rests on NIKE's scale, balance sheet, and visible self-correction. Fiscal 2026 revenue held at $46.4 billion, and North America grew 5% currency-neutral with EBIT up 14% to $5,376 million, showing the core franchise still earns strong returns. Gross margin rose 20 basis points to 42.9%, and ROIC remained 18.7% on the company's own calculation. The balance sheet is strong: long-term debt is rated A+ and A2, cash and short-term investments total $9.0 billion, and management states it has full covenant compliance and expects liquidity to cover needs for the next twelve months and beyond. Management is also acting on the problems the bear cites: it is reducing footwear supply, clearing inventory, and reinvesting in wholesale, with the goal of completing these actions by December 2026. The $986 million IEEPA tariff recovery is a real cash item, with substantially all of the remaining receivable collected after year end. Greater China and Converse are real drags, but they are a bounded share of the business, and the filing says North America has made the most progress. Dividends remain the primary use of cash, and buybacks can resume when conditions allow.

claims.claim: The balance sheet and liquidity support the business
claims.quote: We believe that existing Cash and equivalents, Short-term investments and cash generated by operations, together with access to external sources of funds as described above, will be sufficient to meet our domestic and foreign capital needs for the next twelve months and beyond.

claims.claim: Management is actively repositioning the business to restore momentum
claims.quote: we believe they will reignite brand momentum and reposition our business to drive long-term shareholder value.

bear.argument: The bull case leans on figures that the filing itself qualifies. North America's 14% EBIT gain sits beside a segment where NIKE Direct fell 6% and comparable store sales fell 2%, and North America's gross margin gain was helped by lower product costs and channel mix, not demand. Consolidated EBIT rose only 2%, to $3,850 million, and the 8.3% margin is still far below the 12.7% of fiscal 2024. The $986 million IEEPA tariff recovery flattered cost of sales; excluding it, underlying profitability is weaker than the headline suggests. Operating cash flow fell 22% to $2,868 million after a $1,678 million working capital drag, and $684 million of tariff receivables sat on the balance sheet at year end. The 'bounded' drag is not small: Greater China EBIT fell 20% and Converse EBIT fell 93%, and management says both will weigh through fiscal 2027. Global Brand Divisions still lost $4,603 million. Liquidity is strong, but NIKE paused buybacks and cut shareholder payouts, and the filing lists $15.5 billion of endorsement obligations against a shrinking top line.

claims.quote: a net change in certain working capital components and other assets and liabilities that decreased cash provided by operations by $1,678 million

bull.argument: The opponent is right that the headline numbers need qualifying. North America's EBIT gain was helped by lower product costs and channel mix, consolidated EBIT rose only 2%, and the 8.3% margin is well below fiscal 2024. The $986 million IEEPA recovery also flattered cost of sales. I accept these points. The bull case is narrower: the core North American franchise grew 5% on a currency-neutral basis, and the company has the means to get through a reset. The $684 million of tariff receivables was largely collected after year end, which turns a balance-sheet item into cash. Liquidity is strong: $9.0 billion of cash and short-term investments against $15.5 billion of endorsement obligations, of which only about $1.7 billion is due within 12 months. Management also states it has full covenant compliance. The buyback pause is a choice, not a distress signal, since the filing says repurchases may resume and will be funded from operating cash flow. The filing names dividends as the main financing outflow but does not describe a dividend cut. Greater China and Converse are real drags, and the bull case depends on the reset working by December 2026 as management plans.

judge.reasoning: The bear's claims rest on verified quotes covering margin compression, persistent Greater China and Converse headwinds, and a verified $1,678 million working capital drag that directly undercuts the bull's liquidity framing. The bull concedes several key points in Round 2 and leans on a North America growth figure and a liquidity quote that do not address profitability or cash flow deterioration, so the bear's responses are more complete and better supported.
